question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $4x - y = 1$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $4x - y = 1$, we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4x - y &= 1 \\
-y &= -4x + 1 \\
y &= 4x - 1
\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $4$.

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $4$ is

$$
y = 4x
$$
